## Purpose

Advance one admitted promotion toward its frozen target. It preserves the source
commit exactly, checks the step's trusted CI evidence, publishes a distinct step
attestation, and fast-forwards the target. A versioned step also requires an
annotated tag with the exact promotion identity before completion.

## When a playbook uses it

Use it after the promotion request has frozen its task, batch, member, and retained
source. Only a daemon service may invoke it; sessions have no publication grant.
Repeating the command recovers an interrupted publication from Git observations.

## How it works internally

`IntegrationCommandsMixin` resolves the batch's frozen step to a `DaemonLanes`
promotion lane. `StepAdmission` validates the immutable inputs and retained source.
`PromotionVisit` requires the exact request PR, green boundary checks on S, and
the frozen step's approval policy. Operator approval requires a human repository
administrator; requester approval requires the frozen `requester.github_login`.
The optional frozen `gate.operator_logins` allowlist narrows eligible admins;
being listed never grants permission, and an empty list admits nobody. Repository
permission is observed again at each gate. Lookup failures hold with
`promotion_operator_permission_unavailable`; rate limits reach the train's shared
repository backoff.
The newest decisive review must approve S; a dismissal, changes request, or newer
review on another head withdraws that approval. The lane refreshes the PR and
HostedChecks outside the publication fence before writing.

It publishes the step attestation outside the ref fence, then the branch and tag
with separate exact leases, following the recovery matrix in specification §3.3.
Both writes are recoverable individually. Settlement requires `git_truth` and,
when versioned, the validated tag object and its peeled source.

## Side effects and persistence

The request uses one `task_context` row of type `promotion_intent`; its canonical
JSON contains `request_id`, `repository_id`, `target_ref`, `source_sha`, `base_sha`,
`step`, `version`, `checks_version`, `requested_at`, `requester`, `notes_sha256`,
`pr_number`, and `pr_url`. The requester records the authenticated local identity
and, when available, its bound GitHub login. A notes source requires a SHA-256
digest; `none` uses a null digest. `BatchStore.freeze` accepts
that metadata as `promotion=...` and stores it under
`policy_snapshot.promotion_intent`, alongside `policy_snapshot.promotion_step`,
before sealing. Admission compares the entire intent to this frozen copy;
approval is observed on GitHub and never added to the intent.
The request's approve command must post the review using the operator's own local
GitHub login, never the installation App identity. If that human credential is
unavailable, the request mechanism must stop and ask the operator to provide it.

`StepAdmission.retain(batch, member, request_id)` publishes completion provenance
under generation `promotion:<request_id>`. The request mechanism owns the
create-only `refs/heads/aq/promote/<step>/<request>` ref and its PR. Successful
publication deletes that temporary ref under its own lease, provided its head
still equals S and the target contains S. Later promotion visits retry pending
cleanup of settled batches. The task status, separate `task_metadata` entry
`promotion_result` (batch ID, source SHA, tag OID), and batch settlement are written
in one transaction. The request context stays unchanged; Git remains the delivery
authority. Missing tags recover from target ancestry even after the target
advances or GitHub reports the PR merged.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`promotion_intent_invalid` refuses a non-promotion batch. A held visit explains
tampered or unretained inputs, a non-fast-forward target, or an existing tag with
the wrong type, source, or promotion identity. Existing tags are never replaced.
`unknown` means read-back has not proved delivery and retry remains safe.
`testing` waits for trusted checks on the exact source; red checks hold the
promotion rather than allocating a merge repair. Inspect the returned `detail`
and the promotion task to locate the request inputs.

## Example step

```yaml
command: integration_promotion_publish
args:
  batch_id: "{{ promotion_batch_id }}"
```
